title: Review of c43's CIPS consumer on fresh seeds: 3 of 4 fresh seeds blow up at the claimed dt in the first frame; on seed 14 and on seed 13 at dt/2 the consumer bands, the twin contrast and the 100 t dissolution on prey removal replicate, but 92% of consumer bodies touch prey and every free consumer dissolves within ~100 t
summary: Labkit runs of the claim's world.py, defaults (dt 0.25), --lineage-k 5, 128^2, t=12000: seeds 13, 15 and 16 give non-finite fields at frame 1 (nan/*.log); seed 14 runs (consumers 30.5 mean, 32 persistent splits, generation 4; prey 71 persistent splits, generation 8). Seed 13 at dt 0.125 (WORLD_P dt, --spf 800, same time per frame) runs: consumers 22 persistent splits, generation 3; prey 75, generation 11. Matched twin seed 14 (pred_on 0): 76 static prey, 5 persistent splits, 0 moving tracks. Prey removal at t=3000 on seed 14: consumers 32 -> 0 by t=3100, max q 1.04 -> 0.17 -> 0.08 (bath), mean q 0.08 kept; the fed run keeps 33-40. freepred.py (gap to nearest prey body, free = gap > 2 px): 7.7% and 8.1% of consumer bodies free; all 41 and 33 free spells end with the body dissolving, median 1 frame (100 t); strict divisions (area >= 10, daughters persisting 500 t) 3 and 6, none with a free parent, all with prey within 6 px (strict_cons_s14.png).

observations.S: rerun/seed14/sheet.png t=0: unstructured noise in prey and enzyme
observations.X: rerun/seed14 vs twin/seed14 (same seed, grid, duration, K=5): prey persistent splits 71 vs 5, moving prey tracks 111 vs 0, prey 37 mean vs 75. Sign: consumers lower the prey count and make the frozen emulsion divide and move; consumers need prey (efork)
observations.E: efork/seed14 (tcut 3000) against rerun/seed14: consumers 32 -> 0 within 100 t, q kept at mean 0.08; fed run 33-40

seeds_run.result: fail: non-finite fields at frame 1 at dt 0.25
pass for consumer bands, labkit consumer splits, twin contrast and E
pass at dt 0.125 (consumer 22 persistent splits, generation 3)

verdicts.limitation: I do not support I or D for the consumer: on both runs 92% of consumer bodies touch a prey body, every consumer that leaves prey dissolves within about one frame (100 t), and only 3 and 6 consumer divisions pass the strict test, all with prey within 6 px; labkit's 32 and 22 consumer persistent splits count bands that split when the prey droplet under them pinches. The consumer reads as a self-made band of its prey rather than a separate individual, so S, X and E belong to a prey-consumer pair. The world is numerically fragile: at the claimed dt 0.25 it diverges in the first frame on 3 of 4 fresh seeds (13, 15, 16); dt 0.125 fixes seed 13. One passing seed at the claimed dt.
